notes: Each spot looks like itself: a willow and big lily pads close around you at Lily Cove, a far hazy shore with swells and mist out on the Deep, and willow banks with a quick current at Willow Creek. Rowing between spots shows your boat crossing the lake.

A livelier lake: a heron wading the shallows, a canoe paddling past, big fish leaping, breezes sweeping the water and spring petals falling. Bubble spots are bigger, more frequent and well worth casting at.
Fewer interruptions: fish you've caught before go straight to your basket with a small note, messages queue up instead of piling up, and tips only show when they make sense.

Things happen in the world: Wren waits on your dock with her boat, lanterns are lit at dusk, and new things on your dock are pointed out. A note tells you when a fish you've never caught could bite right now.
The neighbours have more to say, in their own words, about what you've been up to, and they greet you in passing on the street.

New music: a written tune for each season and for dawn, dusk, night and the village, with quiet in between. Snags in the lilies come loose on their own, a missed bite keeps its worm, and you can dig more worms at the dock when the tin runs out.
